reader.requirement: Every explicitly referenced nonunique user-defined name (data-name, condition-name, file-control and entry-clause operand, procedure-name, special register) must be made unique by its written qualifiers; a reference whose qualifiers leave zero or several candidates is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.Cite: only the citation text of the COBOL1639 ambiguity message (1985 IV.4.3.8.1 vs 2023 8.4.2.2.3 SR1); the verdict (one survivor resolves, several is an error) is the same code

DialectLevel >= 2002: from 2002 a data description entry clause operand (ODO data-name-1, SAME AS, OCCURS KEY, RENAMES) takes the groups above its subject as implicit qualifiers; below 2002 the whole scope's candidates are counted, so a name declared beside the subject and in another record must be qualified

ConstructRegistry.Check(QualifiedIndexName2002): a qualified index-name is refused at 85 (COBOL0900); 1985's qualification formats 1-6 name no index-name and VI.5.8.3 SR14 makes index-name-1 unique in the program
Edition.Cite: only the message text of COBOL2121/COBOL2122; the refusal is the same code

reader.edition-search: grep for DialectLevel, Edition.Year, EditionContext, CobolVersion, Permissive and ConstructRegistry in NameResolution.cs, SymbolTable.DataNameCandidates.cs, SymbolTable.IndexNames.cs, SymbolTable.Procedures.cs, SymbolTable.ConditionNames.cs, QualifiedNameClasses.cs, OccursKeyResolvePass.cs, OdoResolvePass.cs, StatementValidation.cs, DataBinder.cs#UniqueOrReportAmbiguous; the grammar rules qualification, dataReference, procedureName and reportGroupReference carry no version predicate
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a data description entry clause operand (ODO counter, OCCURS KEY) gets no implicit qualification, so a name also declared in another record must be qualified (refused unqualified at 85, accepted at 2002); qualified index-names are refused at 85
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb919 covers an ambiguous index-name; data-names, condition-names, file-control keys, entry-clause operands and procedure-names are not exercised

reader.notes: One verdict (UniqueOrReportAmbiguous / DataItemNamed) counts the survivors of the qualifier walk; every probed operand class refuses an ambiguous or misqualified reference (COBOL1639; procedure-names COBOL2121; counters COBOL2729). The 85 arm of ClauseOperandsTakeImplicitQualifiers is right for 1985, whose only exception is redefinition. Minor, not a verdict change: after a refused RECORD KEY a cascade COBOL0864 prints the glued text 'KYOFIREC'.

refuter.evidence: cn4.cob (runs/cn4-001, --std 85): 01 R1. 05 F PIC 9. 88 X VALUE 1. / 01 R2. 05 X PIC 9. Every reference is qualified (IF X OF F, IF X IN R1, DISPLAY X OF R2), so each nonunique name is made unique by qualifiers as SRL2.1 asks. Printed: exit 65, cn4.cob(9,12): error COBOL2692: 'X' names two types of user-defined word in this source element (condition-name and data-name) ... (ISO §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1 ...). The same refusal at --std 2002 and --std 2023 (runs/cn4-002, cn4-003). At 1985 condition-names, data-names and record-names are ONE disjoint set: OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1  the text is in the clause (4. condition-names, data-names, and record-names); and identical names are resolved by qualification: OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1  the text is in the clause; it lies in SR3 (Identical user-defined names may appear in a source program); OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.1  the text is in SRL2.1 (uniqueness must be established through a sequence of qualifiers). Code: DataBinder.cs#CheckOneTypePerWord -> SymbolTable.UserWordCensus#Record -> UserWordKinds.MayBeOneWord, whose shared group MayShareOneName is the 2023 list (constant-name, data-name, property-name, record-key-name, record-name) with no condition-name and no edition arm; only ConflictMessage's citation text varies by edition. The refusal half held: redq.cob (B OF G1 under a REDEFINES sibling, A OF RN through a 66, A OF G2 -> three COBOL1639), ord2.cob (file-name not outermost, a 77 qualified by a file, a repeated file -> four COBOL1639), pn1/pn2/pn3 (ambiguous or misqualified PERFORM, GO TO DEPENDING, ALTER, USE FOR DEBUGGING -> COBOL2121/2122/1639), rw7.cob (GENERATE D with D in two RDs -> COBOL1920), ren1.cob (qualified RENAMES operands accepted: AB A). kb/Work search (COBOL2692 with 1985, 'condition-names, data-names'): no note covers this pair (PB4996, PB5073, PB5482, PB5783, PB5800 concern other matters).

src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#CheckOneTypePerWord: the declaration-time COBOL2692 that pre-empts qualification for a condition-name spelled like a data-name

refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (rejects-legal-source, cause a: 1985 needs an arm of its own). A condition-name and a data-name of one spelling are in one disjoint set at 1985 and are legal when every reference is qualified; the compiler refuses the second declaration with COBOL2692, so the qualified references SRL2.1 admits never compile. The fix site is UserWordKinds.MayBeOneWord (an edition-aware sharing set; at 1985 set 4 = condition-name, data-name, record-name). Repro: cn4.cob; same output at --std 2023 (whether 2023's list justifies it there is not judged here). The primary rule is §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1; this row is overturned because the program it admits is refused.
